Ok - thanks for the info.   I've been running node v0.8.9 with deps/uv patched with this since I sent the original query.

I looks only looks marginally better:

29271 ?        Ssl    0:02 Haraka (master) cn=2428 cc=0 cps=0/0.17/8

29286 ?        Sl     0:12  _ Haraka (worker) cn=290 cc=0 cps=0/0.02/7     

cn=connections handled; cc=concurrent connections; cps=connections per second current/average/maximum

I guess this could be explained by Haraka doing a lot of network I/O e.g. rdns lookups, DNSxL checks etc. at connection start-up and will therefore hit an idle timer almost straightaway?   Plus I guess the OS scheduler will naturally prefer one process??

Would you only expect to see an improvement here when under much heavier loads?
